policy.rule: A blocking external assumption must be proven by an executable repository artifact before public API depends on it.

assumptions.claim: DSH Agent creation preserves the caller-bound Principal-derived context as ownerCtx.
Agent setup runs before Session/Agent publication, so setup failure cannot expose a half-configured Agent.
A derived child Fiber is lifetime-owned by its parent and parent disposal waits for child cleanup.
ctx.inject is dependency-reactive and may rerun after provider loss/recovery; user semantic work therefore requires the non-reactive Operation boundary.
Runtime capability providers preserve Tenant/Principal isolation, descendant inheritance, teardown and unpublished setup semantics.
A Principal-owned Operation captures required capabilities once, does not re-enter semantic work on provider churn, and drains with Principal teardown.

Pinned DSH scopes share the application Cordis root while ToolRuntime registrations remain scope-aware, and the official dsh-mcp-client reserves serverName root-wide; the integration therefore needs a deterministic per-Principal-Session physical namespace.
